identification: Minute, slender straw-colored insects (less than 1.0 mm) with fringed feathery wings found feeding inside leaf sheaths, flower buds, and leaf undersides.
symptoms: Lacerating and sucking of sap causes leaves to curl upwards ('boat-shaped leaves'). Bronze or silvery sheen on lower leaf surface with brown necrotic streaks along veins. Flower buds drop, fruits become scarred with rough skin.
conditions: Hot and dry dry weather spells, bright sunshine, temperatures 28-35°C.
prevention: Erect blue sticky traps @ 20-25 traps/acre (thrips are specifically attracted to blue color). Intercrop with coriander or marigold.
management: Foliar spray with Fipronil 5% SC @ 1.5ml/L or Spinetoram 11.7% SC @ 0.8ml/L or Acetamiprid 20% SP @ 0.3g/L. Bio-pesticide: Verticillium lecanii @ 5g/L.

identification: Microscopic yellowish-green oval mites (0.2 mm) invisible to the naked eye, colonizing the lower surface of tender young leaves.
symptoms: Causes severe downward curling of leaves ('inverted boat shape'), leaf thickening, brittle leathery foliage, petiole elongation ('rat tail symptom'). Distinguishable from thrips because thrips curl upwards while mites curl downwards.
conditions: High humidity (>70%) combined with warm temperatures (25-30°C).
prevention: Avoid broad-spectrum synthetic pyrethroids. Keep field clear of solanaceous weeds.
management: Spray acaricides: Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 1.0ml/L or Fenazaquin 10% EC @ 1.5ml/L or Wettable Sulphur 80 WP @ 3.0g/L. Ensure spray thoroughly covers the underside of the foliage.
